title: Sony Sets November 6 Global Release for Ramayana With Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, and Sai Pallavi
excerpt: The first Indian film to receive the 'Filmed for IMAX' label will get a worldwide theatrical release from Sony Pictures, timed to coincide with Diwali festivities.
body:
• Sony Pictures Entertainment will release Ramayana: Part One in theaters worldwide on November 6, 2026, with India's domestic release through Dharma Distribution following on November 8 to coincide with Diwali.
  • The film marks the first time a Hollywood studio has given a mainstream global theatrical release to an Indian production, with screenings available in 3D and IMAX formats.
  • Ranbir Kapoor stars as Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, and Yash as Ravana, with Oscar winners Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman scoring the film and DNEG handling visual effects.
  • The two-part epic carries a combined budget of Rs 4,000 crore including marketing, with Part 2 slated for Diwali 2027.

Sony Pictures Entertainment has confirmed that Ramayana: Part One will release in theaters worldwide on November 6, 2026, marking the first time a Hollywood studio has given a mainstream global theatrical release to an Indian film. The domestic Indian release through Karan Johar's Dharma Distribution will follow two days later, timed to coincide with Diwali.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=-e9Ukms9tKw

The release date carries deep significance for the source material. Diwali celebrates the return of Lord Rama to his kingdom of Ayodhya after 14 years of exile and his victory over the demon king Ravana — the very story the film brings to the screen.

A Historic Distribution Deal

The Sony partnership represents an unprecedented milestone for Indian cinema's global ambitions. Producer Namit Malhotra of Prime Focus Studios, who is also CEO of the Oscar-winning VFX house DNEG, described the deal's significance in an interview with Collider.

https://x.com/ManozTalks/status/2095873660754219519

"In over 100 years of Hollywood and the Indian film industry, this will be the first film ever that hits mainstream theatrical release worldwide by a Hollywood studio and an Indian movie coming together."

— Namit Malhotra, Producer, Prime Focus Studios

The film will be available in multiple languages including English, with screenings in 3D and premium formats. Ramayana holds the distinction of being the first Indian production to receive the "Filmed for IMAX" label, as the premium format company expands its footprint into Indian cinema.

Scale and Ambition

Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, whose Dangal remains the highest-grossing Indian film ever made, Ramayana: Part One traces the story of prince Rama and his wife Sita during their exile and the events following Sita's abduction by the demon king Ravana. The film is envisioned as a two-part cinematic spectacle, with Part 2 slated for Diwali 2027.

The cast brings together stars from across Indian cinema. Ranbir Kapoor plays Rama, Sai Pallavi plays Sita, and Yash — fresh from his role in Toxic — takes on Ravana. The ensemble includes Sunny Deol as Hanuman, Amitabh Bachchan as Jatayu, Lara Dutta as Kaikeyi, Arun Govil as Dasharath, and Anil Kapoor as Janaka.

The technical team matches the ambition. Oscar winners Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman have collaborated on the score. Action choreography comes from Terry Notary and Guy Norris, while DNEG — the eight-time Oscar-winning VFX studio behind the Dune films and Interstellar — handles visual effects. The combined budget for both parts, including marketing, stands at Rs 4,000 crore.

Global Box Office Prospects

Ramayana enters a competitive November release window alongside Warner Bros.' animated The Cat in the Hat adaptation and Toho's Godzilla Minus Zero, according to The Wrap. Despite that competition, Indian diaspora audiences in the US and internationally are expected to drive significant turnout, building on the crossover success of recent Indian exports like RRR and Kalki 2898 AD.

The film's international marketing has been substantial, including an English-language trailer debut at San Diego Comic-Con in July that showcased nearly four minutes of footage featuring large-scale battle sequences and mythological creatures.

Dharma Productions acquired Indian theatrical distribution rights in a reported Rs 250 crore deal, underscoring industry confidence in the film's domestic commercial prospects. Produced by Prime Focus Studios and Yash's Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is positioned as Indian cinema's biggest release since Baahubali.
